topics.title: Background to Emergency and the economic context

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the Bangladesh crisis, the stoppage of US aid, oil price rise, inflation and monsoon failure created discontent after 1971.
Describe the bitter party competition and the conflicting views of the Congress and the opposition about the judiciary and personal authority.

topics.title: Gujarat and Bihar movements and the Railway strike
topics.ncert_sections: Gujarat and Bihar movements; Railway Strike of 1974

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the causes, course and outcomes of the student agitations in Gujarat and Bihar in 1974-75.
Explain Jayaprakash Narayan's leadership of the Bihar movement and his call for total revolution.
Describe the 1974 Railway strike led by George Fernandes and the government's response to it.
Identify the constitutional issues between Parliament and the Supreme Court that culminated in the Kesavananda Bharati case.
Evaluate the 1973 supersession of judges and the idea of a 'committed' judiciary and bureaucracy.

topics.title: Declaration of Emergency
topics.ncert_sections: Declaration of Emergency; Crisis and response

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the Allahabad High Court verdict of 12 June 1975 and the Supreme Court's partial stay on it.
Explain how and on what grounds Emergency was proclaimed under Article 352 and what powers it gave the government.
Describe press censorship, the bans on organisations and the acts of resistance during the Emergency.
Explain preventive detention and the significance of the April 1976 Supreme Court ruling on habeas corpus.
Identify the constitutional amendments made during the Emergency, including the forty-second amendment.
Assess the strengths and weaknesses of Indian democracy that the Emergency revealed.
State the changes made to the Emergency provision after 1977, including armed rebellion and written Cabinet advice.
Analyse the unresolved issues of the balance between protest and governance and the politicisation of the police and administration.

topics.title: Politics after Emergency: the Lok Sabha elections of 1977
topics.ncert_sections: Politics after Emergency; Lok Sabha Elections, 1977

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the Janata Party was formed and how it turned the 1977 election into a referendum on the Emergency.
Interpret the results of the 1977 Lok Sabha elections and their regional pattern.

topics.title: Janata Government and the legacy of the Emergency

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the factional struggle in the Janata government and the reasons for the mid-term elections of 1980.
Describe how non-Congressism and the politics of backward castes changed the party system after 1977.
Evaluate why the Emergency period is seen as both a constitutional and a more serious political crisis.
